title: Structural Traps — Coordination Problems
metadata_mapping: Existing concept and responsive asset conventions; no new schema, navigation, or publication action.

patterns.title: Coordination Problems
patterns.domain: Strategic and game-theoretic problems; equilibrium selection, expectations, and conventions

sources.title: Schelling, The Strategy of Conflict, chapter 3 (1960)
sources.supports: Tacit coordination of expectations, mutually recognized clues, focal points, and limits of salience.
sources.read_method: Original chapter pages 54–57 read from local scans and OCR; book-cover scan identifies a later edition with new preface. Original work dated 1960.
sources.boundary: Illustrative respondent samples, described by Schelling as unscientific, do not establish universal coordination rates or effects of a modern acknowledgment procedure.

sources.title: Van Huyck, Battalio, and Beil, Tacit Coordination Games, Strategic Uncertainty, and Coordination Failure (1990)
sources.supports: Strategic uncertainty, multiple strict ranked equilibria, distinction between disequilibrium and inferior equilibrium, repeated minimum-effort experiments.
sources.read_method: Published scanned article: introduction, game definition and equilibrium analysis, monitoring treatment, and conclusions read via local OCR.
sources.boundary: Specific laboratory minimum-effort game; not evidence that all repeated or large-group coordination fails. Monitoring improves individual best responses without necessarily selecting the collectively best equilibrium in that setting.

sources.title: Crawford, Gneezy, and Rottenstreich, The Power of Focal Points Is Limited (2008)
sources.supports: One-shot focal-point experiments with symmetric and asymmetric matching rewards; salient labels can lose effectiveness when payoffs favor different outcomes by role.
sources.read_method: Published PDF introduction, pilot and paid X-Y design, treatment payoffs, and results read.
sources.boundary: Pilot used hypothetical payoffs; subsequent treatments paid subjects. Article explicitly refers to paid experiments and makes no numerical rate claim or estimate of acknowledgment effects.

patterns.short_description: Recognize when mutually beneficial action depends on compatible expectations, then distinguish selecting a shared plan from changing incentives, capabilities, or the costs of mismatch.
use_when: Which choices put Mina and Owen together?
goals: Recognize the concrete predicament before terminology.
Preserve defining assumptions and distinctions without calculations.
Evaluate intervention authority, costs, residual risks, and changed assumptions.
mechanisms: Name one usable entrance and time, acknowledge it, and coordinate revisions.
Communication, access, and follow-through remain necessary. Recovery takes additional time or resources.

example_structure.scenario: One meeting; North and South entrances equally feasible and equally preferred; choices before observing the other, no recovery in the first-choice benchmark. Both matching outcomes are equilibria. Acknowledged communication selects an existing outcome; adding recovery changes the model.
example_structure.changed_relationship: Name one usable entrance and time, acknowledge it, and coordinate revisions.
example_structure.residual_constraints: Communication, access, and follow-through remain necessary. Recovery takes additional time or resources.
example_structure.evidence: Hypothetical scenario and stipulated continuation; no expected result presented as measured outcome. Qualitative ranking and ordering replace illustrative arithmetic.

visual.question: Which choices put Mina and Owen together?
visual.alternative_text: Hypothetical qualitative illustration. Mina and Owen can each choose North or South entrance. Both North and both South are double-outlined equilibria; split choices miss the meeting. Neither has an intrinsic preference for an entrance. Naming and acknowledging North selects one existing matching outcome. Change: Name one usable entrance and time, acknowledge it, and coordinate revisions. Limitation: Communication, access, and follow-through remain necessary. Recovery takes additional time or resources.
visual.caption: Hypothetical illustration. The two matching cells are equally acceptable equilibria. An acknowledged entrance and time select one without changing preferences. An unread message, closed entrance, or unconfirmed revision can still defeat the plan.

patterns.evidence_boundary: Foundational definitions and formal results retain their assumptions. Empirical studies retain setting and design limitations. Examples and suggested practical responses are original editorial synthesis. Expected familiarity is an editorial judgment, not a comprehension-study finding.
